Hi Annie —

Hope you had a good weekend. As we start the renewal cadence for Elara, I wanted to surface a structure we think will align with your growth plans while protecting unit economics on both sides. Based on the usage you shared for H1 and the Q3 forecast in the MAP (attached), the ask from your side was: (1) maintain a near-term price hold for 6 months, (2) secure uplift capacity with staged credits, and (3) have an operational true-up every quarter.

High-level proposal (v1):
- 12-month renewal term
- Price hold at current list for first 3 months, then a 60% blended discount on committed units thereafter (details below)
- Tiered rollforward credit: unused committed units in each quarter roll forward as credits up to 2 subsequent quarters; credits decay after that
- Optional 6-month uplift option at fixed uplift rate if actual usage exceeds committed band by >30%

Can we get a quick alignment call this week to walk through the MAP and the credit lifecycle? If this looks directionally good I can loop in Finance (Marissa) and get a formal draft term sheet out.

Lauren / Marissa —

I modeled three permutations and attached a short calc tab (I dropped it into the shared drive link):
A) 6-month hard price hold, then blended discount at 60% on committed units; credits roll forward 2 quarters, cannot be used for uplift purchases. Expected margin impact: -6.2% NRR
B) 6-month hard price hold, credits usable for uplift purchases up to 25% of uplift volume; credits convert to dollar offsets at 50% value after 2 quarters. Expected margin impact: -9.4% NRR (but materially reduces churn risk)
C) 3-month partial price hold (list unchanged but elevated committed discount for months 4–6), credits usable for any purchases, conversion to dollar offset at 75% after 2 quarters. Expected margin impact: -12.1% NRR — our most conservative pricing cushion.

My recommendation is B for the following reasons: (1) preserves a safety net for them during migration, (2) limits credit exposure for us (25% cap), and (3) conversion to dollar offsets at 50% reduces long-term liability while giving them balance-sheet relief.

If you agree I will prepare a short term-sheet draft (redwood-term-sheet-draft-2027-08-10.pdf) we can send to Annie for review. Marissa, if Finance signs off I can include a clause that triggers an optional uplift at fixed uplift rate (24% over committed unit price) if they exceed the threshold.
